questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.**

Gratification
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is Contentedness.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Gratification **refers to the feeling of satisfaction or pleasure that comes from achieving a desired goal or fulfilling a desire.

 
 
• For example, if someone has been working hard to finish a project, they may feel a sense of gratification when they finally complete it.
 
 
 
• **Option 1, "Contentedness", **is a suitable **synonym **for gratification as it also refers to a state of satisfaction and happiness.
 
 
• For example, if someone is content with their life, they are satisfied and happy with what they have.
 
 
 
• **Option 2, "Dejection"**, is the opposite of gratification, as it refers to a feeling of sadness or disappointment.
 
 
• For example, if someone fails to achieve a goal, they may feel dejected.
 
 
 
• **Option 3, "Pique"**, refers to a feeling of irritation or resentment, usually caused by someone else's actions.
 
 
• For example, if someone makes a rude comment, it may cause pique in the person who hears it.
 
 
 
• **Option 4, "Dispiritedness",** refers to a feeling of low spirits or lack of enthusiasm.
 
 
• For example, if someone is feeling dispirited, they may lack the energy or motivation to do anything.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

questions.question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.**

"Where have you put the medical kit?” I asked my nephew.

options.text: I asked my nephew where he had put the medical kit.
I asked my nephew that where he had put the medical kit.
I asked my nephew where had he put the medical kit.
I asked my nephew where he has put the medical kit.

questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is** ​I asked my nephew where he had put the medical kit.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in **direct speech. **We need to change it into **indirect speech.**
 
• **Commas **and **inverted commas** are removed.
 
• The reported verb **'asked' **remains unchanged.
 
• **'Wh'** word remains the same in this conversion.
 
• The position of subject and verb interchanges i.e. **'have you' **becomes** 'he had'.**
 
• The **present perfect tense 'have put' **changes to **past perfect tense 'had put'.**
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

**Correct Indirect Speech:__* ****I asked my nephew where he had put the medical kit.*

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.**

Native
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"Foreign".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Native"** refers to something or someone that belongs to a particular place or country, or is a characteristic or inherent quality of a person or thing.

 
 
• For example: "She is a **native **of New York" or "The **native **language of Japan is Japanese."
 
 
 
• **"Foreign" **is the **opposite **of **"native"** and refers to something or someone that comes from a different place or country.
 
 
• For example: "He speaks a **foreign **language fluently" or "The restaurant serves **foreign **cuisine."
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **"Innate"** means something that is inherent or natural, present from birth or inherent in a person or thing.

 
 
• For example: "Her **innate **talent for music was evident at a young age."
 
 
 
• **"State"** refers to a political division within a country, or can also mean the condition or quality of something.
 
 
• For example: "The **state **of California is located on the west coast of the United States" or "The **state **of the economy is concerning."
 
 
 
• **"Distant"** means something that is far away in space or time, or has a lack of closeness or intimacy.
 
 
• For example: "The nearest gas station is too **distant **to walk to" or "He has a **distant **relationship with his father."
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9074044cf96dc1d09ca89eac99180c3d7440ade1b364d09d47931959bf693cc8.png] **Confusion Points__**

 
• **'Distant' **is not an antonym of '**native**' because they are not opposites in meaning.
 
• '**Distant**' means far away or remote, while 'native' refers to something or someone that belongs to a particular place or was born in a particular place.
 
• These two words have unrelated meanings and are not opposite to each other.

**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Hang in there
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **Don’t give up.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct meaning of the idiom **"Hang in there"** is **2) Don't give up**.
 
• It is an expression **used to encourage someone to persevere through difficult or challenging times, to not give up, and to keep going.**
 
 
• Example: "I know you're going through a tough time, but **hang in there**. Things will get better."
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is **Option 2.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1) There is no chance - **This is not the correct meaning of the idiom "Hang in there." It suggests that there is no possibility of success or improvement.

 
 
• Example: "I'm sorry, but **there's no chance **you'll be able to get a refund for that item."
 
 
 
• **Option 3) Let go of your stand **- This is not the correct meaning of the idiom "Hang in there." It suggests giving up on one's beliefs or convictions, which is opposite to the idea of perseverance.
 
 
• Example: "I know you're passionate about this issue, but maybe it's time to **let go of your stand **and try to compromise."
 
 
 
• **Option 4) Put your ego aside - **This is not the correct meaning of the idiom "Hang in there." It suggests suppressing one's ego or pride, which may be necessary at times, but it is not the main idea of the idiom.
 
 
• Example: "I understand you're upset, but if you want to resolve this issue, you need to** put your ego aside** and listen to what the other person has to say."

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

________ being a good actor, he is also an amazing singer.
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **Besides.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The most appropriate option to fill in the blank is **1) Besides.**
 
• The sentence structure is indicating that the second clause is meant to add an additional piece of information about the subject, not to present a contrast or opposition.
 
• Therefore, the word** "Besides" **is the best choice as **it is used to indicate that something is in addition to what has already been mentioned.**
 
 
• *Example: "**Besides **being a good actor, he is also an amazing singer." This sentence indicates that the person being referred to is not only good at acting but also has a talent for singing.*
 
 
 
• **Option 2) But **is not appropriate in this context as it indicates a contrast or opposition between two clauses.
 
 
• *Example: "He is a good actor, **but **he is not a good singer." This sentence indicates that the person being referred to is good at acting, but not good at singing.*
 
 
 
• **Option 3) Beside** is not appropriate in this context. This preposition means "next to" or "alongside."
 
 
• *Example: "I sat **beside **my friend at the movie theater." This sentence indicates that the speaker sat next to their friend in the theater.*
 
 
 
• **Option 4) Also** is not appropriate in this context. It is an adverb that indicates that something is in addition to something else, but it doesn't connect the two clauses in a grammatically correct way.
 
 
• Example: "He is a good actor. **Also**, he is an amazing singer." This sentence is grammatically correct, but it presents the two pieces of information as separate sentences rather than as clauses connected by a conjunction or preposition.
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is Option 1.

**Correct Sentence:**__ *__**Besides**__ being a good actor, he is also an amazing singer.*

questions.question: What is the role of conservation canines?
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is **Sample Detection.**

• The role of conservation canines, as mentioned in the passage, is **to assist scientists in their research by detecting samples. **These samples may include whale faeces, as in the case of Tucker, or other genetic and physiological information that is used to tackle conservation problems around the world.
 
• This is supported by the following lines from the passage: *"Conservation canines are fast becoming indispensable tools for biologists...Her organisation’s dogs and their handlers are fully booked to assist field researchers."* **(Paragraph 2)**
 
• Additionally, the passage also states that the ideal detection dog is motivated by the expectation of a ball game as a reward for sample detection. This further emphasizes the role of detection dogs in detecting and retrieving samples for research purposes.

• It also mentions how conservation canines are used to study a number of species, including right whales and killer whales, and how their sense of smell is used to non-invasively collect genetic and physiological information.
 
• Additionally, the passage discusses how these dogs are rescued from shelters and given a satisfying career in conservation research.
